title: getting your driver's licence
objectives: List B.C.'s driver licence classes and identify which vehicles each class lets you drive
Identify which vehicles require an air brake endorsed driver's licence
Describe the steps to get a commercial driver's licence, an air brake endorsement or a heavy trailer endorsement
State the prerequisites (age, driving record, medical) for applying for a Class 1, 2, 3 or 4 licence
Explain what happens during the road test, including the pre-trip inspection

sections.title: Licence classes and what each allows
points: Class 1 covers semi-trailer trucks and all other vehicles or combinations except motorcycles.
Class 2 covers buses, including school buses; trailers over 4,600 kg allowed only if bus and trailers have no air brakes.
Class 3 covers trucks with more than two axles, like dump trucks, plus tow cars and mobile truck cranes.
Class 4 unrestricted covers buses up to 25 persons including driver, taxis, limousines, ride-hailing vehicles and ambulances.
Class 4 restricted covers taxis, limousines, ride-hailing and special vehicles up to 10 persons including the driver.
Heavy trailer endorsement (code 20) allows trailers over 4,600 kg if neither truck nor trailer has air brakes.
You must hold a full-privilege Class 5 or equivalent before applying for a commercial licence or trailer endorsement.
mustKnow: Minimum age: 19 for Class 1, 2 and 4; 18 for Class 3 and heavy/house trailer endorsements
Class 2 and 3 trailer limit: trailers or towed vehicles may not exceed 4,600 kg (may exceed only if no air brakes)
Class 4 unrestricted bus limit: maximum seating capacity of 25 persons (including the driver)
Class 4 restricted: up to 10 persons including the driver
House trailer endorsement is code 07 (formerly code 51); heavy trailer endorsement is code 20

check.q: What is the minimum age to apply for a Class 3 licence?
check.explanation: Class 3 has a minimum age of 18, while Classes 1, 2 and 4 require age 19.

check.q: A Class 4 unrestricted licence lets you drive a bus with a maximum seating capacity of how many persons, including the driver?
check.explanation: Class 4 unrestricted covers buses with a maximum seating capacity of 25 persons including the driver.

sections.title: Medical fitness, vision and keeping your licence
points: Commercial applicants must declare medical conditions and have a doctor complete a Driver's Medical Examination form for RoadSafetyBC.
Commercial drivers must meet a higher vision standard than Class 5 drivers; vision is screened at a driver licensing office.
Vision checks cover visual acuity, peripheral vision, depth perception, double vision and colour perception (red, green, amber).
If you need glasses or contact lenses to meet the standard, you must wear them during vision screening.
RoadSafetyBC requires regular medical exams as long as you hold a commercial licence; missing the form can cancel your licence.
RoadSafetyBC can also require re-examination: vision screening, knowledge test, or a road test with pre-trip inspection.
mustKnow: Routine medical reports are due at ages 25, 30, 35, 40 and 45; then 48, 51, 54, 57, 60 and 63; then every year from age 66
The doctor's fee for the routine medical form is not covered by MSP of B.C., ICBC or RoadSafetyBC
Colour perception test: ability to distinguish red, green and amber

check.q: From what age must commercial drivers submit a Driver's Medical Examination Report every year?
check.explanation: The manual states the medical form is required every year upon reaching the age of 66.

check.q: Who pays the doctor's fee for completing the routine medical form?
choices: The Medical Services Plan of B.C.
check.explanation: The fee is not covered by MSP, ICBC or RoadSafetyBC, so the driver pays it.

sections.title: Air brake endorsement, heavy trailer endorsement and MELT
points: Operating air brake vehicles on a highway (except construction vehicles) requires an air brake endorsement (code 15).
The endorsement is also required for most vehicles with air-over-hydraulic brakes; code 15 appears under licence restrictions.
To get code 15: complete an air brake course, pass the knowledge test, then pass an air brake pre-trip inspection test — no road test.
A certified air brake course adds 4 hours of practical pre-trip training and may exempt you from ICBC's pre-trip test.
All new Class 1 applicants must take MELT; air brake training is included, so no separate course is needed for Class 1.
MELT is a one-time requirement; Class 3 or 2 applicants instead need air brake experience or a course before the road test.
Drivers with a licence issued outside Canada must take B.C.'s MELT; some Canadian experience can waive it.
mustKnow: Air brake courses are a minimum of 7 hours in length
Air brake knowledge test results are only valid for one year
Failing the air brake knowledge test after three attempts means completing or repeating an approved 7-hour course
MELT became a requirement for all new Class 1 applicants on October 18, 2021
MELT waived with more than 24 consecutive months of Canadian Class 1 experience (licence not expired more than three years)

check.q: How long are air brake knowledge test results valid?
check.explanation: If the endorsement isn't placed on your licence within one year of passing, you must re-take the test.

check.q: What is the minimum length of an air brake course?
check.explanation: Air brake courses are a minimum of 7 hours; certified courses add 4 hours of practical training.

sections.title: Applying step-by-step and knowledge tests
points: Prerequisites: full-privilege Class 5 or 6 (or equivalent), acceptable driving record, minimum age, no outstanding fines, and medical standards.
Acceptable record means fewer than four penalty-point offences in two years and zero motor-vehicle Criminal Code convictions in three years.
Apply at a driver licensing office with primary and secondary ID, pay the fee, and take the knowledge and road signs tests.
The learner's licence lets you practise with a supervisor seated beside you (or immediately behind and to the right).
With a learner's licence in a bus, taxi, ride-hailing vehicle or ambulance, only your supervisor and same-class learners may ride.
All knowledge tests are multiple choice, conducted only in English, and every answer is in this guide.
After passing the road test you get a temporary licence and a medical form your doctor sends to RoadSafetyBC.
mustKnow: Driving record: fewer than four offences carrying penalty points in the previous two years
Driving record: zero motor-vehicle-related Criminal Code convictions in the previous three years
The learner's licence is valid for one year
The supervisor must be at least 19 years old and hold the appropriate licence class for the vehicle
Heavy trailer endorsement supervisor: at least 19 years old and holds a Class 1, 2 or 3 driver's licence

check.q: How long is a commercial learner's licence valid?
check.explanation: The learner's licence is valid for one year and allows practice with a supervisor.

check.q: How many motor-vehicle-related Criminal Code convictions are allowed in the previous three years?
check.explanation: Applicants must show zero motor-vehicle-related Criminal Code convictions in the previous three years.

sections.title: Road tests and the pre-trip inspection test
points: All road tests include a pre-trip inspection, an air brake pre-trip inspection (if equipped) and the road test itself.
Under the National Safety Code, pre-trip inspections must always be done before the first run of the day.
During the inspection, tell the examiner what you're checking and complete a written trip inspection report.
You must demonstrate starting, stopping, shifting, turning, steering, backing, parking, merging, exiting and driving in traffic.
Class 1 and code 20 tests add coupling and uncoupling a tractor unit from a trailer.
Bring a safe, representative, properly licensed and insured vehicle; unsafe vehicles get the test cancelled.
Passing with an automatic transmission restricts a Class 1, 2 or 3 licence to automatics only.
mustKnow: A Class 1 road test takes about two hours; Class 2, 3, 4 and heavy trailer tests take less than two hours
No-show fee applies without 48 hours notice or a valid reason; arrive at least 15 minutes early
Class 1 test vehicle: loaded tandem/tridem tractor-trailer with air brakes, on-road loaded weight at least 28,000 kg
Class 1 semi-trailer must be at least 13 metres long (7.5 metres if pintle hitch trailer)
Heavy trailer endorsement test: trailer with its load must weigh at least 4,600 kg, no air brakes

check.q: About how long does a Class 1 road test take?
check.explanation: A Class 1 road test takes about two hours; other commercial tests take less than two hours.

check.q: How much must the loaded Class 1 road test vehicle weigh on the road, at minimum?
check.explanation: The Class 1 test requires a loaded tractor-trailer with an on-road loaded weight of at least 28,000 kg.

summary: Each licence class (1-4) covers specific vehicles, with minimum ages of 19 (18 for Class 3) and a full-privilege Class 5 prerequisite.
Air brake vehicles need a code 15 endorsement; trailers over 4,600 kg without air brakes need a code 20 heavy trailer endorsement.
The application path is: knowledge and signs tests, learner's licence, supervised practice, road test with pre-trip inspection, then medical form.
All new Class 1 drivers must complete MELT, a one-time course that includes air brake training.
Keeping a commercial licence means regular medical reports on a set age schedule and re-examination whenever RoadSafetyBC asks.
